title: Network Delay Time
statement: `times[i] = [u, v, w]` is a directed edge from u to v with travel time w. Nodes are labeled 1..n. A signal starts at node `k`. Return the time until every node has received it, or -1 if some node is unreachable.
hints: This is single-source shortest paths on a graph with positive weights.
Dijkstra with a binary heap computes those distances.
The answer is the maximum finite distance. An infinite distance means return -1.

approaches.name: Bellman-Ford
approaches.explanation: Relax every edge n - 1 times. No negative weights, so it is correct.

approaches.name: Dijkstra
approaches.explanation: The right tool for nonnegative weights.

editorial: Build the adjacency list and a distance array initialized to infinity, with dist[k] = 0. Pop the closest unsettled node and relax its outgoing edges. A stale heap entry, whose distance does not match the array, is ignored. The delay is the max distance. If any node is still infinite, the signal never arrives.

examples.explanation: Every node receives the signal by time 2.
Node 1 never receives a signal that starts at 2.
